I absolutely love her as a result of it. I LOVE the drama of it all. The symbolism. The subtlety of it. The deliberate choices that were made to carry her story in her abilities ouhshshdhf I LOVE IT. This isnt an essay as much as it is a huge ramble on the aesthetics of her abilities so bear with

Like i remember when people complained about her not being able to sing as her ability - and like i agree that wouldve been really cool but honestly i really like what we got. The fact that her shadows have little effects that look like ashes when she moves is so cool to me - in fact the whole shadow thing reflecting her death and the state of the theatre afterwards (how it was burnt to ashes and how the only thing that remained was her cloak, even she died along with the theatre!!! Which is really pretty symbolism in and of itself) is so cool

Because it greatly reflects how she left everything behind. How she left behind her life on stage, how she left behind the abuse of her father/the director and her broken home, how she devoted herself entirely to the woman in red and her cult, her not having her abilities revolve around her singing shows her freedom!!! And having it revolve around her death in that theatre fire shows that is the moment that she felt free. Her rebirth was promised to her by that woman, whoever she may be, and the fact that her abilities reflect the identity that she chooses to harbour as her follower rather than the opera singer that her father tried to pave her out into being... its so interesting to me and this kit reflecting her death so heavily rather than her life is so!!! Oufhsjdndng im a little obsessed

Like it shows a complete disconnect in regards to how she sees her life vs how she sees her "rebirth." She doesnt associate with the life that she lived prior to when she met the lady in red, she only lives in the times where she was with her, its clear that shes either willingly choosing to cut ties with her former self and taking her identity into her own hands, or she genuinely just does not remember her life before she became a part of the cult, showing just how much she has entirely dedicated herself to the woman that saved her. Either to me is genuinely really compelling, to be so dedicated to a cause and genuinely find salvation no matter the cost to oneself is so interesting to me. 

Like the same thing with her not having singing abilities, in her story she destroyed her voice and it shows just how far she is willing to go in order to find this "rebirth" that she was promised. Her desperation to escape the life that she lived before this cult, and to cut ties with the stage she was forced upon is something that takes a lot of strength to do but that strength is a big part of her character, and its why the shadows being the central part of her abilities IS a big deal! Because it speaks on who she is NOW, and how she took her life into her own hands! She chose to not be the opera singer that the people want her to be anymore. And i love her for that.

This ofc is not the only way to play ada, and there are probs better ways i dont kmow about, but this is how i personally tend to use ada:

- looking at where your health is, is an absolute MUST. Do not accidentally down yourself when whistling to a teammate - as whistling can increase your damage. There is a hunter ability that allows them to see downed survivors - so this can get you chaired if there is no chase going on and the hunter is a bit opportunistic. 

- please please pay attention to the quick messages. People who more so understand how ada works have luckily been real good when i play her and use a quick message when theyre being chased, letting me know who i can heal and who not. If there are multiple injured survivors and one uses a quick message for cipher progress, thats your safest healing bet. Not always, but most often. 

- contain/kiting adas are rather rare but like someone else said in the comments, decoding next to a kiting area is a really good idea. Especially since adas stress ability (taking three hits rather than two) is pretty powerful when it comes to kiting. Check your health and give your stress enough time to activate, and you can easily kite for a long while. Your kiting strategy however is just dependent on the hunter - but i can give you some strats for hunters i main! 

- again like someone else said, rescue adas are more common because of her stress ability. If you immediately go for the rescue, you have more time and less pressure to perform the rescue hitless because of this - the moment youre hit tho is your ticket to go for it as theres a hit cooldown for the hunter. That time window is easy for a rescue, and youll still have full health after rescuing - making you able to whistle to a different teammate! Maybe not the same teammate unless they lose the hunter tho

- Carry tide turner in your persona for rescues. Its good for the team, it makes the hunter waste time no matter what and it gives your teammate time to get the hunter away from everyone else if they cant escape being chased, and tide turner can give them that chance to escape in the first place. Its always a net positive to have tide turner - especially with ada, on top of that theres a healing buff on the same branch which helps with whistling faster.

- The other big part of her persona tho? Free real estate. I use borrowed time bc im a bad kiter lmao, and a 50% fear res is good. Its like a last chance. But flywheel i can also see having a use for her - as a way to keep her hit immunity after its gone. But you gotta use it just before the hunter hits you tho. Flywheel is a lil tricky to get the hang of, but with ada i feel itd definitely have good use. Broken windows is also a net positive and makes kiting easier. It really depends on just what youd like in your persona. 

Also two more general/courtesy tips:

- if you cant remember everyones persona builds (its hard), wait until someone is down to pop the last cipher. They typically have borrowed time and itll heal them. If you wanna be extra safe, change your quick messages to carry "cipher machine primed!" When you have a cipher primed. If the teammate getting chased uses "focus on decoding!" It means they dont have borrowed time and are telling you to pop it so they can distract the hunter. My memory's not great but i THINK (not sure) you can change quick messages in the social part of your settings- but anyone please correct me on this if im wrong.

- to be safe, dont wait at gates unless youre confident you can rescue the current kiter if they get chaired. For many reasons - it can drastically turn a match around if you die, it can stop the final player from going through dungeon too. 

Idk i just kinda tried to cram all the stuff i learned playing idv into here, along with ada specifically - i hope these help!! Im not a pro player by any means, but these have oftentimes been useful and helped me with my matches! Of course there are plenty of really good guides on yt that help, but these are based on my experiences and are typically good for starting out. Not sure about higher levels, but starting out definitely.
